summary: David Schaberg is a scholar in sinology who studied at Stanford University (~1982–1986) and Harvard University (~1989–1996). He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1996.

David Seyfort Ruegg worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris and EHESS under Jean Filliozat, Louis Renou, Marcelle Lalou, and Rolf Alfred Stein, and held professorships at Leiden, Washington, and Hamburg.

David Shulman is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1967–1971) and the University of London (~1972–1976). He served as Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1976–2016).

David Tracy worked in religious studies and philosophy, studying at Saint Joseph's Seminary (~1956–1960) and the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1960–1969). He held posts at the Catholic University of America and as professor at the University of Chicago (~1969–2006).

David W. Chappell worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, completing doctoral work at Yale University (~1968–1976). He was a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1972–2000) and later held a post at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

David W. Tien is a scholar in sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Toronto, McGill University, and the University of Michigan, studying under Robert H. Sharf and doctoral supervisor James Robson.
David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

Dawa Norbu worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from the University of Delhi (~1970–1974) and UC Berkeley (~1976–1982), and held posts at San Francisco State University, University of San Francisco, CIIS, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1986–2006).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Oriental College, Lahore (~1899–1903). He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935) and as Director of Archæology and Historical Research in Jaipur State (1935).

Dayong was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Taixu, Bai Puren, and Palden Tenzin Nyendrak. He studied and taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1923) and founded the Tibetan Language School of Beijing.
Debala Mitra was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Director at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1952–1983).
Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He served as director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages in 1988.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was an Indologist and historian of philosophy who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1937–1942) under Surendranath Dasgupta, later holding a post at the University of Calcutta.
Deborah Carlson is an archaeologist who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology, both attested in 2015.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Vienna and Harvard University under Oleg Grabar (~1970–1976), and served as a professor at the University of Vienna (~1990–2014).
Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Renmin University of China (~1996–1999), where he became associate professor of religious studies (~2002).

Denis Twitchett worked in sinology and history, studying at SOAS and St Catharine's College. He served as professor at the University of London (~1960–1968) and the University of Cambridge (~1968–1980), and held an emeritus post at Princeton University (~1980–1994).

Denma Lochö Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery (~1940–1953). He served as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (~1978–1979).
Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).
